subQuestions.questionText: Provide a definition of the word humility (line 1).
subQuestions.memoText: Humility could be defined as being humble/modest/having a lack of pride.

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to paragraph 1.

Explain, in your own words, what the writer states about current leaders.
subQuestions.memoText:
They are pompous/arrogant (1) instead of being humble (1), as expected./They are arrogant/self-important (1) because they think too highly of themselves (1) as leaders.
[Award only 1 mark for lifting.]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the contrasting views presented by the writer in paragraph 3.
subQuestions.memoText:
The writer distinguishes between humble and arrogant leaders: humble leaders acknowledge others' views and accept their flaws, whereas egotistical leaders ascribe their mistakes to other employees, rather than taking accountability.
[Award 2 marks only if the contrast is discussed.]
[Award only 1 mark for lifting.]

subQuestions.questionText: Account for the use of the rhetorical question in paragraph 4.
subQuestions.memoText: The rhetorical question convinces the reader to consider the writer's view./The rhetorical question challenges the reader.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the appropriate response from the list of options below.

The writer's tone in paragraph 5 is …

A forceful.
B argumentative.
C assertive.
D persistent.
subQuestions.memoText: C – assertive

subQuestions.questionText: Is the writer objective in paragraph 6? Motivate your response by a close reference to this paragraph.
subQuestions.memoText:
The writer is not objective in his assessment of the appointment of leaders. The first two assertions are followed by a statistic, 'The overlap between confidence and competence is just 9%'. However, this apparent statistic is not backed up by any evidence nor has this information been accredited to any source./The writer's subjectivity is also evident in the italicised word, 'think'. His information is based on supposition, 'There may be some', which is not grounded in fact.
[Credit valid alternative responses.]

subQuestions.questionText: With reference to ONE example, discuss how the writing style in paragraph 7 reinforces the role of charisma in leadership.
subQuestions.memoText:
• The concept of charisma is highlighted by metaphors that allude to the sense of sight, 'blinded' and 'magnifies'. This allusion stresses the importance of charisma when leaders are appointed.
• The use of emotive words that convey intimacy ('seduced'/'charming'/'enchanting'/'entertaining showmen') further highlight how charisma is used as a tool of manipulation.
• The writer also juxtaposes the adjectives 'all' and 'no' in the expressions 'all style and no substance' and 'no style and all substance' to criticise the unreasonable/shallow criteria used to appoint leaders.
[Award 1 mark for the identification of the writing style and 2 marks for the discussion.]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the writer's assertion, 'We are too lazy to evaluate talent' (line 36), in the context of paragraph 8.
subQuestions.memoText:
The writer states that we make a superficial evaluation based upon observation rather than on considering the leader on the basis of actual intellectual ability and skill. This assertion is justified by the argument that skills have evolved and so are more difficult to assess. The writer's statement that some people are simply 'clueless' about talent, implies a sense of laziness with regard to the evaluation of suitable candidates.
[Award 3 marks for a well-developed discussion.]

subQuestions.questionText: Comment on the writer's repetition of the pronoun 'we' in the concluding paragraph.
subQuestions.memoText:
The writer repeats 'we' to include readers as active participants in combatting arrogance in leaders. The readers are persuaded to acknowledge the necessity of changing their mind-set in respect of leadership qualities./The passage concludes by asserting that the promotion of humility in leaders is a collective responsibility – we have to be advocates for humility.
[Award 3 marks only if a comment is made.]

subQuestions.questionText: With close reference to the woman's body language in FRAMES 1 and 4, discuss her attitude towards Rudy (the man).
subQuestions.memoText:
In FRAME 1, the woman seems to be impressed by Rudy's memoir. This is evident in her clutching the page and leaning forward. After hearing that the memoir was fictitious, the woman appears to be nonchalant/dismissive in FRAME 4. This attitude is revealed by her tucking the book under her arm, raising her shoulders and turning her back on him.
[Credit candidates who see the woman's attitude as being in denial/oblivious to his confession in FRAME 4.]

subQuestions.questionText: Comment on what is revealed about the man in FRAMES 3 and 4.
subQuestions.memoText:
The man (Rudy) is unapologetic about the misrepresentation of his abilities in his memoirs and unashamedly exploits others' gullibility. This reveals that he is self-absorbed/vain/egotistical. He is scathing of others who believe his portrayal of himself despite his acknowledging that his memoirs were not true.
[Award 3 marks only if a comment is made.]

subQuestions.questionText: Critically discuss the extent to which TEXT B supports paragraphs 9 and 10 of TEXT A.
subQuestions.memoText:
In paragraph 9 of TEXT A, the writer argues that people equate arrogance with strong leadership; humility is seen as a 'feminine attribute' (paragraph 10). People are impressed by men who boast and show off even if they are dishonest. He further explains that arrogance and lying are celebrated and glorified, when flaunted by men.
TEXT B supports paragraphs 9 and 10 of TEXT A by showing that blatant arrogance and self-promotion are esteemed by others. The fact that a woman is expressing praise for her male colleague, who has admitted to the lies in his memoir, links to the gender stereotypes described in TEXT A. Furthermore, the woman's submissive/acquiescent demeanour reinforces the view that women are 'unfit for leadership' (paragraph 10) because she does not challenge the man's duplicity.
[Award 4 marks for a critical discussion of paragraphs 9 and 10 of TEXT A and TEXT B.]

subQuestions.questionText:
TEXT C discusses the value of being resilient. Summarise, in your own words, the benefits of being resilient.

**NOTE:**
1. Your summary should include SEVEN points and NOT exceed 90 words.
2. You must write a fluent paragraph.
3. You are NOT required to include a title for the summary.
4. Indicate your word count at the end of your summary.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark allocation:
- 7 marks for 7 points (1 mark per main point)
- 3 marks for language
- Total marks: 10

Accepted points:
1. Resilient people are able to adapt to changing circumstances.
2. Those who have mastered their struggles are able to endure and develop positively.
3. The willingness to accept assistance from others is an indicator of resilience.
4. Being resilient allows people to recognise and embrace their emotions.
5. Resilient people are more self-aware.
6. Overcoming difficulties allows for personal growth.
7. Resilience empowers individuals to resolve challenges.
8. Accepting situations that are beyond one's control can help one prioritise situations within one's control.
9. Positivity enables one to anticipate better outcomes.
10. A resilient person's fears are allayed by focusing on their aspirations.

Distribution of language marks when candidate has not quoted verbatim:
- 1–3 points correct: award 1 mark
- 4–5 points correct: award 2 marks
- 6–7 points correct: award 3 marks

Distribution of language marks when candidate has quoted verbatim:
- 6–7 quotations: award no language mark
- 4–5 quotations: award 1 language mark
- 2–3 quotations: award 2 language marks

Word Count: Markers are required to verify the number of words used. Do not deduct any marks if the candidate fails to indicate the number of words used or if the number of words used is indicated incorrectly. If the word limit is exceeded, read up to the last sentence above the stipulated upper limit and ignore the rest of the summary.

subQuestions.questionText: Why does the advertiser use the pronoun 'you/your' in the text of the advertisement?
subQuestions.memoText: The advertiser appeals to the reader directly./The reader is being challenged.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss what is conveyed by the advertiser's choice of phrases: 'more dentists' and 'all other toothpastes combined'.
subQuestions.memoText: The phrases convey that Crest is recommended by most dentists (1) which implies that it is a superior brand (1).

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the written text: 'When you get … in your favour.'

Comment on ONE technique used by the advertiser to promote the product.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Emotive diction: The advertiser's choice of emotive diction ('fighting'/'dramatically'/'battle') is persuasive in that it creates fear and panic to act with urgency and use Crest to prevent cavities.
• Endorsement by experts: 'dentists' choice' highlights the claim that expert opinion favours the use of Crest toothpaste.
• Statistics: The use of statistics ('523 million cavities since its introduction in 1955') validates the claim that Crest is a superior product and it prevents the formation of cavities.
• Litotes: The advertiser wants to promote the authenticity of the information in the advertisement and the effectiveness of the product ('there's no second chance'/'no sure things').
• Personification: The advertiser uses the expressions, 'Crest for fighting cavities' and 'Crest helps put the odds in your favour' to highlight the effectiveness of the product.
• Personal pronouns: By using the pronouns, 'you' and 'your', the advertiser engages the readers in order to convince them of the benefits of the product.
[Award 1 mark for the identification of ONE technique and 2 marks for a comment.]

In FRAME 6, Jeremy's mother reacts with dismay/contempt when he demands an 'EXCUSE NOTE'./She is offended by his disparaging statement that expressing gratitude is a waste of time.
[Award 3 marks only if a comment is made.]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss how the cartoonist uses satire in his presentation of Jeremy.
subQuestions.memoText:
Jeremy expresses gratitude to his mother for all the work and assessments she has completed on his behalf, revealing his lazy and exploitative nature./All Jeremy's claims of being grateful are nullified by his thoughtless comments in FRAME 6, which reveal his selfish motive for complimenting his mother./The cartoonist ridicules Jeremy's self-absorbed nature and the manner in which he exploits his mother.
[Award 3 marks only if there is an understanding of satire.]
